author: @Yigtwxx

evidence.api_compatibility: The change alters server behavior for a specific error condition: a backend that returns 200 OK on text/event-stream but sends zero SSE data events now emits a framed data: {"error":...} event with status_code 502 instead of a synthetic data: [DONE]. Clients that previously saw an empty-but-successful completion will now see an error. This is a correctness fix (a failed generation was being hidden as success) rather than an intentional API change, so it is unlikely to break clients, but it is worth noting in release notes as a behavior correction.
evidence.documentation: No documentation changes. The behavior correction (empty streams now reported as errors instead of success) may warrant a brief note in release notes, but no spec or guide updates are required as this fixes a silent bug rather than introducing new documented behavior.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No maintainer to-do: the bug was reported in production (@pdittaro on ds4:rocm), and the unit tests comprehensively cover all classification branches. The error-path is exercised by the mock backend hitting a 200 with no SSE events; the acceptance path is exercised by multiple event shapes. CI has an additional check called 'check' that failed, but the PR merged cleanly through GitHub's merge queue and all other CI steps (build on multiple platforms, benchmarks, dependabot) passed — investigate whether that single failure is relevant to this change.
evidence.post_approval_commits: First approval was at 2026-09-01T18:35:05Z. One commit was added after that approval: the refactor to parse_field() (36e7917, 2026-09-09). This was a direct response to @Geramy's review comment requesting the safer approach, implemented between inline review comments, and the branch received a new approval from @Geramy at 2026-09-13T04:24:44Z. No commits were added after the latest approval. The post-approval work was well within the spirit and scope of the original PR.
evidence.review: Three reviewers engaged substantively: @fl0rianr identified three SSE edge cases (optional space after colon, blank-line terminator tracking, CR/CRLF support) across two comment rounds; @abn (subject area: telemetry, HTTP) approved with detailed analysis and two non-blocking follow-up nits; @Geramy (subject area: sockets, TCP/IP) requested a refactoring to a shared parse_field() helper to avoid hardcoded substr offsets, which was implemented. @jeremyfowers reviewed test file scope and prompted reduction from 233 to 210 lines. The PR body and commit messages reference AI-assisted development (Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 across four commits) with session links; verify this is consistent with the project's ai-content-policy.md.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change is strictly about error reporting in the SSE proxy. No credential handling, auth changes, network calls, or permission broadening.
evidence.tests: New file test/cpp/test_streaming_silent_stream.cpp (210 lines) covers two categories of streams: five accepted shapes (LF terminators, no space after colon, CR terminators, bare data field, ChatCompletionChunk) and four rejected shapes (empty stream, unframed backend output, unterminated event, comment-only). Also includes a unit test for the CRLF split-holdback in process_sse_lines() and a regression test for duplicate [DONE] markers. The PR description states that without the fix, the empty-stream and unframed-output cases fail with the exact log lines from the original report. No tests were weakened or deleted.

subject: fix(server): report backend streams that end without any SSE event (#3448)
summary: Fixes a server-side bug where backend SSE streams returning HTTP 200 without any data events were incorrectly reported as successful empty completions instead of errors, and hardens the SSE parser to handle optional colon spacing and CR/CRLF line terminators.
verdict_reason: The fix is narrow, well-tested, and thoroughly reviewed by two subject-matter experts (@abn on HTTP/telemetry, @Geramy on networking), with all post-first-approval changes addressed during the review process and CI passing.
